build: Ocean type 1 cartridge, 16 banks of 8 KB (128 KB)

comments.text: Fine horizontal scroll, 0 to 7: set_view_window subtracts it from 7 and adds the result to scroll_x times 8. $88C1 combines it with $10 into $07AF.
Fine vertical scroll, 0 to 7: set_view_window subtracts it from 7 and adds the result to scroll_y times 8. $88C8 combines it with $10 into $07AE.

The joystick bits, written once a frame by update_player: the low four bits of CIA 1 port A (or port B when A reads $7F). Bit 0 is up, bit 1 down, bit 2 left, and bit 3 right, with 0 meaning pressed; $0F means nothing is pressed. The player code that update_player runs (from $8603, and also $8EAF, $905F, and $AF4F) compares it with $07 (right), $0B (left), $0D (down), $0E (up), and combinations such as $05, $06, $09, and $0A; it is also read at $06E3.

Which handler update_player runs through player_mode_step: 0, 1, or 2. The setup at $500A sets 2 when bit 7 of the stage record's byte is set; other writes are in the player code. Mode 0 is walking and jumping: player_mode_step ($85DC) sets fire_flags and runs $8603 and $89A9, which read joy_bits, and $08FA is zero on the ground and non-zero in the air. Mode 1 runs $9025 and then $919E; $9055 reads joy_bits for up, down, left, and right, and the action number $0905 is 6. Mode 1 is entered at $8A2F and $8B09 (with $0B set to 1 and $0905 set to 5, when the tile checks at $9D3C all show bit 5, value $20) and at $881D and $8D4B (with $0B at 0), and the third sprite is switched on again when mode 0 returns at $90C8 and $9108. Mode 2 runs $8E88, which sets $0905 to 7, turns the eight joystick directions into the movement mask $0D, and calls the scroll requests $42E1 (left), $42F8 (right), $430F (up), and $4326 (down); it is entered at $8B37 when the tile check finds bit 6 (value $40), with $08FA at $FF and $08FB at $30, and the jump or fall step at $8F12 applies while $08FA is non-zero. Mode 0 is restored at $8FDD, $9237, $9258, $92A1, $92D2, $9B85, and $A632 (the last one when the player is hit). Also read by player_pose ($413A), set_idle_aim ($9F05), player_fire ($AF3E), and the contact code at $A5B7. What the tile bits in modes 1 and 2 stand for in the game is not yet known.
Where the screen redraw for a one-tile scroll has got to: $FF is idle, 0 lets scroll_draw_edge draw, and 1 is set by $4B8A when the tile step happens. $888D counts it down and acts on 1 and 0.

Direction of the pending one-tile scroll for scroll_draw_edge: 0 up, 1 up-right, 2 right, 3 down-right, 4 down, 5 down-left, 6 left, 7 up-left ($FF none). Set by the routines at $433D-$438B ($FF with scroll_phase when idle); $888D uses it to pick a routine from the table at $0324/$032C.
How many logical sprite entries the tables at $0808-$0880 hold: place_player_sprites sets it, object_sprites_and_hits adds to it (never past $16).
The highest position used so far in sprite_y_buckets ($7CBD).

Index of the first stage object update_objects and object_sprites_and_hits look at. update_objects moves it past objects retired at the front. Loaded at $93A0 from byte $17 of the record at the pointer $26 (0 in the play snapshot).
One past the last stage object: the loops over the stage's objects stop here. Loaded at $93A5 from byte $18 of the record at the pointer $26 ($1A in the play snapshot).

Index of the first of the nine short-lived objects of the pool that update_temp_objects runs. Loaded at $4F4B from byte $18 of a record found through the word table at $0D22 and the byte at $0C06 (it is $4C in the play snapshot).
temp_first + 9, one past the pool, set at $5062.
Left edge of the screen in 8-pixel character columns (16 bits, high byte at $1D). set_view_window multiplies it by 8.
Top edge of the screen in 8-pixel character rows (16 bits, high byte at $1F). set_view_window multiplies it by 8.
Left edge of the visible stage in pixels (16 bits, high byte at $41), set by set_view_window.
Top edge of the visible stage in pixels (16 bits, high byte at $43), set by set_view_window.
Right edge of the visible stage in pixels (16 bits, high byte at $45): view_left + $12F.
Bottom edge of the visible stage in pixels (16 bits, high byte at $47): view_top + $9F.

Player hit box 1, built by object_sprites_and_hits: left edge (16 bits, high byte at $4D). Right edge is $4E/$4F, top $50/$51, bottom $52/$53. Box 2 follows at $54/$55 left, $56/$57 right, $58/$59 top, and $5A/$5B bottom.

Set by copy_sprites_to_tables to the sort-list position of the last sprite it copied when it stopped after eight slots, and to 0 when it reached the end of the list (also written at $4F12 and read at $4112). When it is non-zero, wait_nmi points the raster interrupt at $95A4, to show the sprites left over: sprite_reuse_irq gives them each the first hardware sprite that has become free.
Copy six consecutive directory entries, X stepping by 8 from the value in A.

Copy one entry of the cartridge directory into RAM. Selects bank 0 ($80 to the Ocean bank register $DE00), reads the entry at $8009+X (source bank, source address, destination, length), then switches to the source bank and copies.

Non-zero while the player is hit or dying. The value is set to 1 at $8B7A and $8E14 (the tile check finds bit 1, harmful) and to $FF at $82C9 and $A638, and cleared at $4F04 on stage start. While it is set, player_animate ($98F3) shows a fixed shape, player_fire ($AF34) does nothing, and $89A9 restores the previous position.

Aim direction of the player's shots, 0 to 9: 0 up (facing right), 1 up-right, 2 right, 3 down-right, 4 down (facing right), 5 down (facing left), 6 down-left, 7 left, 8 up-left, 9 up (facing left). Written by player_fire ($AF34), set_idle_aim ($9F05), and $B1CF; read by player_fire to place the shot with the offsets at $0334 and by $4154 and $4182.

Number of the stage section that holds the player. Set from the stage record at $500E, and changed by track_stage_section ($92DF) when the player moves into the next or previous section; the record address is in ($26). Also written at $884C.
The bit mask object updates AND with an object's $3484 byte to decide whether it moves this frame: $FF when bit 7 of $94 is set, otherwise the single bit $029E[frame_count AND 7].

The player's X on screen in sprite coordinates (16 bits, high byte $029C): player_x minus view_left plus $20, worked out by player_sprite_coords and written to sprite 0's X at $40A7. update_view_scroll compares it with zone_left and zone_right.
The player's Y on screen in sprite coordinates, written to sprite 0's Y at $81C2. update_view_scroll compares it with zone_top and zone_bottom.

Eight bytes, $01, $02, $04, $08, $10, $20, $40, $80: one bit for each value 0 to 7. update_objects picks move_mask from it by the low three bits of frame_count, and copy_sprites_to_tables uses it as the bit of each hardware sprite slot.
Table indexed by a sprite count: $00, $01, $03, $07, $0F, $1F, $3F, $7F, $FF, the sprite-enable mask with that many sprites on.
The raster interrupt nmi_frame installs each frame: handler $07AB/$07AC into $FFFE, line $07AD into $D012. The main loop sets irq_panel at line $D5, or $95A4 when $6B is set.
Image of the X high bits ($D010) for the sprites in the tables at $07B4-$07E6.
Image of the sprite-enable mask ($D015) for the sprites in the tables at $07B4-$07E6.
Image of the sprite expand mask for the sprites in the tables at $07B4-$07E6. The main loop copies it to $07BE ($818E), and nmi_frame writes that to $D017 and $D01D ($4D7C, $4D7F).

Sprite colours of the hardware sprite table (the table's first group: colours, then pointers at $07C7, free-lines at $07CF, and X and Y pairs at $07D7), filled by copy_sprites_to_tables and place_third_sprite.
Sprite pointer values (shape block numbers) of the hardware sprite table.

For each slot of the hardware sprite table, a line below the sprite: Y + $16 (Y + $2B for a double-size one) from copy_sprites_to_tables, Y + $15 for slot 0 from place_third_sprite. Probably the line from which the slot can be reused.
X and Y of each slot of the hardware sprite table, two bytes per slot (X at the even offsets, Y at the odd ones).
Colour of each logical sprite entry (one byte each, up to $16 entries). Bit 7 means the sprite is double size.
Height in lines of each logical sprite entry: $15 or, with colour bit 7, $2A.

Sprite pointer value of each logical sprite entry. place_player_sprites puts $FC and $FD here for the player's first two sprites; the third sprite's $FE goes straight into hardware slot 0 (place_third_sprite) and is not in this list.
X low byte on screen of each logical sprite entry.
X high byte on screen of each logical sprite entry.
Y on screen of each logical sprite entry. place_player_sprites adds an entry only for Y $1A to $D3; object_sprites_and_hits adds one for Y below $D5 and not above the object's own limit in $3ABD.
Non-zero while a timed player effect runs (see player_effect_tick). Only ever set to 0 in the traced code.
Bit 7 flashes at the end of the player effect (see player_effect_tick); player_pose reads it.
X position of the player's third sprite in the stage (16 bits, high byte at $08B4), set by player_pose from player_x and an offset in the frame record.
Y position of the player's third sprite in the stage (16 bits, high byte at $08B6), set by player_pose.
The player's X position in the stage in pixels (16 bits, high byte at $08B8).
High byte of player_x ($08B7). Used for the section probe at $930A, the sprite position at $9FC8, and the saved position code.
The player's Y position in the stage in pixels (16 bits, high byte at $08BA).
High byte of player_y ($08B9). Used for the section probe at $9319, the sprite position at $A016, and the moves at $9ADC and $9B7B.
The player's X saved by save_player_x ($08BC is the high byte); restore_player_x copies it back.
The player's Y saved by save_player_y ($08BE is the high byte); restore_player_y copies it back.

The fire state of the player. Bit 6 is the fire button copied by update_player (1 means not pressed, 0 pressed) and bit 7 means the player is shooting. In mode 0 player_mode_step sets $40 when fire is not pressed, otherwise $00 while $08FA is non-zero and $80 when it is zero; player_fire sets $80 when it starts a shot. While bit 7 is set set_idle_aim ($9F05) is skipped and, in mode 1, the movement handler at $9055 returns at once.
Ticks left in the player effect: player_effect_tick decrements it on every second frame and ends the effect when it reaches zero. No other store to it was found in the traced code.

Pixels the view moves in one scroll step. update_view_scroll sets it to 2 on every call, and scroll_up and scroll_down raise it to 4 when the player is $2C or more pixels outside the zone on that side.
The stage, 0 to 4: zeroed by game_start, incremented at $81B1 when a stage is cleared.
Shape number of the player's first sprite (0 for none). Its data is loaded to $FF00 at $50BB; set by $98F3 and player_pose.
Shape number of the player's second sprite (0 for none), whose data is loaded to $FF40 at $50DC.
Shape number of the player's third sprite, set by player_pose; its data is loaded to $FF80 at $509C.
Set by the frame's interrupt, cleared by the main loop: the main loop runs once for each time it changes.

Cleared by game_start ($8037). update_player ($8588) increments it, and the background colour ($D021), on every frame that joystick 2 is held up with fire while joystick 1 is held down with fire. While it is non-zero and stage is below 4, read_keys ($5308) answers the Commodore key alone (column 7 reads $DF) by storing $FF in obj_state of the object number in $08CC. The main loop tests bit 5 of that byte after wait_frame ($81A5) and, when it is set, increments stage ($81B1) and goes on to the next stage: a hidden stage skip.

Scroll mode of the current section, copied from byte $16 of the section record by load_section_record. Read by update_view_scroll: bit 7 clear, the section scrolls horizontally by itself; bit 7 set and bit 6 clear, vertically by itself; both set, the view only follows the player. Bit 5 gives the direction of the automatic scroll (set: right or down, clear: left or up). Bits 0 to 3 are handled by load_section_record.

Edges of the section that the view has reached: bit 0 top, bit 1 bottom, bit 2 left, bit 3 right. update_view_scroll stores the edge when a one-axis scroll toward it has no room left; every scroll step then clears the bit of the opposite edge. load_section_record clears it.

The action number of the player, which player_animate ($98F3) reads together with the facing flag $18. The movement code writes 1, 3, 5, 6, and 7: mode 1 uses 6 (vertical) and 5 (horizontal), mode 2 uses 7, and jumps and falls use 3.
Right edge of the follow zone (16 bits, high byte $0907), in the sprite coordinates of player_screen_x. Loaded from bytes 2 and 3 of the section record.

Left edge of the zone in which the player can stand without the view following (16 bits, high byte $0909), in the sprite coordinates of player_screen_x. Loaded from bytes 0 and 1 of the section record by load_section_record.
Top edge of the follow zone, in the sprite coordinates of player_screen_y. Loaded from byte 4 of the section record.
Bottom edge of the follow zone, in the sprite coordinates of player_screen_y. Loaded from byte 5 of the section record.
Non-zero when place_third_sprite shows the third sprite. Written in several places by the player routines.

Load one stage's set from the cartridge directory: copy entry X, then X+8, X+16 and on, until an entry whose flag bit 5 marks it packed; that one is unpacked in place by bank 0's unpacker at $8DA2, which returns to the caller. X comes from the per-stage table in bank 0 at $8127 ($88, $A0, $B8, $D0, $E8).

Start a stage: bring the cartridge into view ($01 = $37, bank 0), load the stage's set with stage_load, load directory entries 6 and 7, copy a page of bank 13 to $FD00, read the stage's record in bank 5 into $08E3-$08E6, point $3A and $3C at the tables named in the unpacked block's header ($0C1C, $0C1E), then hide the cartridge again.
Queue sound effect number A: unless $DF is non-zero, and while fewer than three effects are waiting, store it at $91 + $90 and add one to $90. Y is preserved (via $8F). sound_frame plays the queue.
Once a frame, from irq_panel: unless $DF is set, play each sound effect queued in $91 onward ($90 counts them) through $6633, then run the sound driver at $6787.

Colour of each character code, 256 bytes, indexed by the character (screen code) found in the screen buffers. recolour_screen copies the entry for every one of the 840 playfield characters into colour RAM. Only the low nibble reaches colour RAM, and a value of 8 or more turns on multicolour for that character, since the playfield runs in multicolour text mode ($D016 bit 4).
Object type in the top three bits and hit points in the low five bits: player shots take hit points off (see object_sprites_and_hits).
Index of each object's current frame record in the tables the pointers $3A and $3C (low and high bytes) point to.
Bit mask of the frames in which the object moves: an object moves when it shares a bit with move_mask.

State bits of each object (stage objects and the temporary pool share the tables). Bit 7 ($80): off screen, not drawn. Bit 6 ($40): set when the object is in the view, but update_objects also sets it, with bit 7, for an object above or below the view. Bit 5 ($20): retired. Bit 1 ($02) makes update_objects skip an object on frames it does not move. Bit 3 ($08) and bit 2 ($04) are tested in update_temp_objects; $FF marks an unused slot.

Flags of each object. Bit 7: a parent whose position followers take. Bit 6: a follower. Bit 4: retire when leaving the view. Bit 5 is tested before calling $B1F7. When an object is destroyed (code at $A7A1), the low four bits choose a routine from the tables at $A868 and $A871.
A follower's X offset from its parent (signed byte).
A follower's Y offset from its parent (signed byte).
X position in the stage of each object, low byte (high byte in obj_x_hi).
X position in the stage of each object, high byte.
Y position in the stage of each object, low byte (high byte in obj_y_hi).
Y position in the stage of each object, high byte.
Left edge of each object's hit box, low byte (high byte at $3C31). Right $3C8E/$3CEB, top $3D48/$3DA5, bottom $3E02/$3E5F; set by set_object_hitbox.
Right edge of each object's hit box, low byte (high byte at $3CEB).
Top edge of each object's hit box, low byte (high byte at $3DA5).
Bottom edge of each object's hit box, low byte (high byte at $3E5F).

Motion state of each object for object_arc_step: 0 is none; with bit 7 set it jumps (bit 6 clear) or falls (bit 6 set); any other non-zero value is an offset into the path data at the pointer $32, and the path move clears it when the path ends.
Counter that object_arc_step uses to step through its speed tables.
Life of each pool object, counted down by one by update_temp_objects on each frame the object moves (set to $18 when one turns into its short animation).

Choose the player's current animation frame and place the extra parts that depend on it. Depending on player_mode ($09), the facing bit 3 of $18, the animation number $0297, and state flags ($08FA, $0900, $0299, $0B), it finds a frame record (through the pointer tables at $0A4B-$0A91, or the fixed records at $0A29, $0A3A, $095D, and $0962) and then: sets the shape number player_shape_3 ($08EC) from the record's first byte (plus 20 and colour $0E in $0916 while bit 7 of $08B2 is set, otherwise plus 10 while the countdown $08DF is not negative, which it decrements); sets the third sprite's position ($08B3/$08B4 and $08B5/$08B6) to player_x and player_y plus an X and a Y offset from the record (chosen by $0902) and $0322/$0323; and loads the extents $031E-$0321 from the tables at $03F7, $040B, $0401, and $0415 indexed by the record's first byte. In mode 1, with $0B zero and bit 7 of $08C6 set, it also loads player_shape_1 and player_shape_2 ($08EA, $08EB) from bytes 9 and 10 of the record.
Put the player back at the position saved by save_player_x and save_player_y: Y first (restore_player_y), then X.
Copy player_prev_x ($08BB/$08BC) back to player_x ($08B7/$08B8).
Copy player_prev_y ($08BD/$08BE) back to player_y ($08B9/$08BA).
Save the player's X position ($08B7/$08B8) in player_prev_x ($08BB/$08BC).
Save the player's Y position ($08B9/$08BA) in player_prev_y ($08BD/$08BE).

Work out the visible part of the stage in pixels from the scroll position. $40/$41 (view_left) = scroll_x ($1C/$1D, in 8-pixel columns) times 8 plus 7 minus scroll_fine_x ($06); $42/$43 (view_top) = scroll_y ($1E/$1F, in 8-pixel rows) times 8 plus 7 minus scroll_fine_y ($07) (the subtraction at $429F starts with the carry clear, so its 8 acts as 7); $44/$45 (view_right) = view_left + $12F; $46/$47 (view_bottom) = view_top + $9F. Every routine that compares a position with the screen (the object updates, the sprite placement, the hit tests) reads these.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 0 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 1 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 2 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 3 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Mark the scroll idle: $0F and scroll_phase $0E both become $FF.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 4 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 5 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 6 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 7 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.

Entry that sets up a map-row copy at map position ($1C/$1D minus 1, $1E/$1F minus 1): stores the results in $20/$21 and $22/$23, the odd-column and odd-row flags in $08C7 and $08C8, and the destination pointer from $08C1/$08C2 into $E5/$E6, then jumps to map_row_copy_start.

Entry that sets up a map-row copy at column $1C/$1D and row $1E/$1F plus $15 (21): column flag goes to $08C7, row flag to $08C8, and destination is $08C1/$08C2 plus $0320 in $E5/$E6. Falls through to map_row_copy_start.
Same as draw_bottom_row_x_plus0 but the column is $1C/$1D plus 1. Reached only from outside this range; the preceding clc and bcc skip past it.
Same as draw_bottom_row_x_plus0 but the column is $1C/$1D minus 1.
Common tail of the three bottom-row entries: row = $1E/$1F + $15 into $22/$23 with its low bit in $08C8, and destination = $08C1/$08C2 + $0320 into $E5/$E6.

Finds the map cell: loads row ($22/$23) shifted right once, uses it as an index into the pointer tables at ($2A) and ($2C) for the row's address, and adds column ($20/$21) shifted right once to get the cell pointer in $E1/$E2. Sets $E9 to $13, then chooses the even path when $08C7 is 0 or the odd path otherwise.

Even-column path loop: multiplies the cell value by 4, adds the block table base $2E/$2F, adds 2 when $08C8 is set (picks the lower pair of the 4-byte block), then copies two characters to ($E5), advancing $E1/$E2 by 1 and $E5/$E6 by 2 until $E9 underflows after 20 passes (40 characters).
Return from the even path.

Odd-column path: copies only the right-hand character of the first block, then copies the left-hand character of the block 20 cells further on ($14 offset) to destination offset $27, sets $E9 to $12, and jumps into the even loop. Locates the block the same way (cell value times 4 plus $2E/$2F, plus 2 for odd rows).

Move the view by one step toward where it should be; called every frame from track_stage_section while the player is not hit. First it sets scroll_step to 2. Bits 7 and 6 of section_scroll_flags then choose the mode. Bit 7 clear: auto_scroll_horizontal, which scrolls right (bit 5 set) or left (bit 5 clear) until the section limit, then follows the player vertically. Bit 7 set and bit 6 clear: auto_scroll_vertical, down (bit 5 set) or up, then follows the player horizontally. Both set: follow_player_both. Following means that a player_screen_x or player_screen_y outside the zone makes the view scroll toward that side. A limit reached is stored in view_pinned_edges, and the scroll then goes idle through stop_scroll.

Section that scrolls sideways by itself. With bit 5 of section_scroll_flags set, room_to_scroll_right is asked and the view scrolls right while there is room; otherwise room_to_scroll_left and a scroll left. At the limit the view is pinned (pin_view_right or pin_view_left), view_pinned_edges gets $08 or $04, and the code falls into follow_player_y.
Follow the player vertically: player_screen_y below zone_top ($090A) scrolls up (try_scroll_up), at or beyond zone_bottom ($090B) scrolls down (try_scroll_down), and inside the zone the scroll stops.

Bit 7 of section_scroll_flags is set. With bit 6 also set the view follows the player in both axes (follow_player_both). Otherwise the section scrolls vertically by itself: bit 5 set asks room_to_scroll_down and scrolls down while there is room, bit 5 clear asks room_to_scroll_up and scrolls up. At the limit the view is pinned (pin_view_bottom or pin_view_top), view_pinned_edges gets 2 or 1, and the code falls into follow_player_x.

Follow the player horizontally: player_screen_x beyond zone_right ($0906) scrolls right (try_scroll_right), below zone_left ($0908) scrolls left (try_scroll_left), and inside the zone the scroll stops.

Follow the player in both axes. The horizontal position is tested first (beyond zone_right, below zone_left, or inside) and then the vertical one (above zone_top, below zone_bottom, or inside). Outside on one axis only gives a straight scroll; outside on both gives a diagonal one through try_up_right, try_up_left, try_down_right, or try_down_left. Inside on both axes stops the scroll.
Scroll up if room_to_scroll_up allows; otherwise pin the view at the top (pin_view_top), store 1 in view_pinned_edges, and stop the scroll.
Scroll down if room_to_scroll_down allows; otherwise pin the view at the bottom (pin_view_bottom), store 2 in view_pinned_edges, and stop the scroll.
Scroll right if room_to_scroll_right allows; otherwise pin the view at the right edge (pin_view_right), store 8 in view_pinned_edges, and stop the scroll.
Scroll left if room_to_scroll_left allows; otherwise pin the view at the left edge (pin_view_left), store 4 in view_pinned_edges, and stop the scroll.

The player is above and to the right of the zone. With no room to scroll up the view is pinned at the top and scrolls right only; with no room to scroll right it is pinned at the right edge and scrolls up only; with room on both sides it takes the diagonal scroll_up_right.

The player is above and to the left of the zone. With no room up the view is pinned at the top and scrolls left only; with no room left it is pinned at the left edge and scrolls up only; with room on both sides it takes scroll_up_left.

The player is below and to the right of the zone. With no room down the view is pinned at the bottom and scrolls right only; with no room right it is pinned at the right edge and scrolls down only; with room on both sides it takes scroll_down_right.

The player is below and to the left of the zone. With no room down the view is pinned at the bottom and scrolls left only; with no room left it is pinned at the left edge and scrolls down only; with room on both sides it takes scroll_down_left.

One step of the view to the right. If the scroll direction $0F is not 2 yet, set_dir_right makes it 2 and the step waits for the next call. The step is skipped while the previous tile's redraw is still too recent: the fine position scaled by scroll_step (fine_x_steps or fine_y_steps) has to be above scroll_phase. The step clears the left bit of view_pinned_edges and subtracts scroll_step from scroll_fine_x ($06). When that goes below 0 the value wraps into 0 to 7, scroll_x ($1C) grows by 1, and tile_scroll_done starts the redraw.

One step of the view to the left, the mirror of scroll_right (direction 6, set_dir_left). It clears the right bit of view_pinned_edges and adds scroll_step to scroll_fine_x ($06); when scroll_fine_x is 7 it first prepares scroll_x minus 1 in $20/$21, and a result of 8 or more wraps into 0 to 7 and stores that value into scroll_x before tile_scroll_done.

One step of the view up (direction 0, set_dir_up). It waits like scroll_left, sets scroll_step to 4 when the player is $2C or more pixels above zone_top, clears the bottom bit of view_pinned_edges, and adds scroll_step to scroll_fine_y ($07). When scroll_fine_y is 7 it first prepares scroll_y minus 1 in $22/$23, and a result of 8 or more wraps into 0 to 7 and stores that value into scroll_y ($1E) before tile_scroll_done.

One step of the view down (direction 4, set_dir_down). It waits like scroll_right, sets scroll_step to 4 when the player is $2C or more pixels below zone_bottom, prepares scroll_y plus 1 in $22/$23, clears the top bit of view_pinned_edges, and subtracts scroll_step from scroll_fine_y ($07). Going below 0 wraps the value into 0 to 7 and stores scroll_y plus 1 before tile_scroll_done.

Diagonal step up and to the right (direction 1). A diagonal only runs when the fine positions are in step, 8 minus scroll_fine_y equal to scroll_fine_x. When they are not, the view scrolls right by itself (scroll_right) until they are. The first instructions work out scroll_x plus $26 and throw the result away.
The jump at $4A04 to scroll_up; no branch or jump in the code reaches it.

The move of the diagonal up and to the right. It keeps only the top and right bits of view_pinned_edges, subtracts scroll_step from scroll_fine_x and adds it to scroll_fine_y. When scroll_fine_x goes below 0 both wrap into 0 to 7, scroll_x grows by 1, scroll_y shrinks by 1 (a subtract with the carry left clear), and tile_scroll_done runs.
Diagonal step down and to the right (direction 3), allowed when scroll_fine_y equals scroll_fine_x. Otherwise the view scrolls right by itself (scroll_right) until they are equal.
The jump at $4A68 to scroll_down; no branch or jump in the code reaches it.

The move of the diagonal down and to the right. It keeps the bottom and right bits of view_pinned_edges, subtracts scroll_step from both fine positions (they stay equal), and when they go below 0 wraps them and adds 1 to both scroll_x and scroll_y before tile_scroll_done.
Diagonal step down and to the left (direction 5), allowed when 8 minus scroll_fine_y equals scroll_fine_x. Otherwise the view scrolls left by itself (scroll_left) until they are.
The jump at $4AC7 to scroll_down; no branch or jump in the code reaches it.

The move of the diagonal down and to the left. It keeps the bottom and left bits of view_pinned_edges, subtracts scroll_step from scroll_fine_y and adds it to scroll_fine_x. When scroll_fine_y goes below 0 both wrap into 0 to 7, scroll_x shrinks by 1, scroll_y grows by 1, and tile_scroll_done runs.

Diagonal step up and to the left (direction 7), allowed when scroll_fine_x equals scroll_fine_y. Otherwise the view scrolls left by itself (scroll_left) until they are equal. The first four instructions are two compares whose branches lead to the next instruction.
The jump at $4B3E to scroll_up; no branch or jump in the code reaches it.

The move of the diagonal up and to the left. It keeps the top and left bits of view_pinned_edges and adds scroll_step to both fine positions. When they reach 8 or more both wrap into 0 to 7 and scroll_x and scroll_y shrink by 1 before tile_scroll_done.

The view has moved by one whole tile. Flip the displayed screen buffer $10 (the old value goes to $11), swap the bytes at $08C0 and $08C2, and set scroll_phase to 1 so that the redraw of the new edge starts (see scroll_phase).
Return with the N flag clear when the view can still move right: the largest view_left in the section record (bytes 8 and 9 at ($26)) is above view_left.
Return with the N flag clear when the view can still move left: view_left is above the smallest view_left in the section record (bytes 6 and 7).
Return with the N flag clear when the view can still move down: the largest view_top in the section record (bytes 12 and 13) is above view_top.
Return with the N flag clear when the view can move up by a whole scroll_step: view_top minus scroll_step is not below the smallest view_top in the section record (bytes 10 and 11).
Return scroll_fine_y ($07) divided by 1, 2, or 4 for a scroll_step of 1, 2, or more. The scroll routines compare the value with scroll_phase to decide whether the redraw has got far enough.
Return scroll_fine_x ($06) divided by 1, 2, or 4 for a scroll_step of 1, 2, or more, for comparison with scroll_phase.
Pin the view at the top limit: scroll_fine_y becomes 7 and view_top is rounded down to a multiple of 8.
Pin the view at the bottom limit: scroll_fine_y becomes 7 and view_top is rounded down to a multiple of 8 (the same code as pin_view_top).
Pin the view at the left limit: scroll_fine_x becomes 7 and view_left is rounded down to a multiple of 8.
Pin the view at the right limit: scroll_fine_x becomes 7 and view_left is rounded down to a multiple of 8 (the same code as pin_view_left).

NMI/IRQ frame handler (nmi_frame). Saves A and the CPU port ($01), maps I/O in with $01=$35, then reads CIA2 $DD0D: if bit 7 is clear (not an NMI) it jumps to frame_exit $4D42. Otherwise it reads state byte $08B0: negative leaves, 0 goes to blank_screen_exit $4D3D, non-zero saves X and Y in $7C/$7D. A value of 1 skips the sprite copy and goes to wait_and_set_vic $4D9A. A value of 2 or more falls into copy_sprite_shadows $4D47.
Branch target after the CIA2 check shows an NMI. Loads $08B0 and picks between exit (negative), blank_screen_exit (zero) or the frame update (positive).
When $08B0 is 0, writes $57 to VIC $D011 (screen control, ECM on) and falls into frame_exit. No sprite or colour work is done for this frame.
Common exit of nmi_frame: pulls the saved $01 value and A from the stack and returns with RTI.

Full frame update, taken when $08B0 is 2 or more. Disables interrupts, then loops X from 7 to 0 copying shadow buffers: $07E7,x to the sprite pointers $CBF8,x and $CFF8,x (both screens), $07EF,x to zero page $6C,x, $07F7,x to $D000,x and $07FF,x to $D008,x (the sprite position registers $D000-$D00F, X and Y alternating) and $07BF,x to sprite colours $D027,x. Then writes the enable mask $07BD to $D015, the X high bits $07BC to $D010 and the expand flags $07BE to both $D017 and $D01D. Sets the next interrupt: $07AB/$07AC (raster_vector) go to $FFFE/$FFFF, line $07AD goes to $D012, and the raster flag in $D019 is acknowledged.

Reached from nmi_frame when $08B0 is 1, or by falling through from the sprite copy. If $D011 bit 7 (raster line high bit) is clear, it waits in a loop until the raster passes line $FB, so the VIC register writes below happen in the lower border.

Writes $00 to CIA2 $DD00 (VIC bank 3, $C000-$FFFF), then applies the shadow registers: shadow_d018 $07B0 to $D018, bg_colour0-2 $08C3-$08C5 to $D021-$D023, shadow_d016 $07AF to $D016 and shadow_d011 $07AE to $D011. Increments frame_flag $08F7 so the main loop sees a new frame, restores X and Y from $7C/$7D, restores $01 and A, and returns with RTI.

Patches game code and data for the current stage ($08E7); called once from round_start at $80A8, after the raster vector is set. Stage 0: sets bytes $213E=$BC and $2150=$C1, sets pointer $48/$49 to $000A, then copies 32 bytes from $20C0 to $C780 unless bit 5 of $35A8 is set, in which case the buffer is cleared. Other stages are handled by the branches below. Returns with RTS.
Stage 0 with $35A8 bit 5 set: fills the 32 bytes at $C780-$C79F with $00 (Y from $1F down to 0), then returns.
Stage is not 0: compares it with 1 and goes to stage_not1 $4E34 if different.
Stage 1: stores $08 at $2D32, sets pointer $48/$49 to $1FC8, copies $201B to $2E87 and $202E to $2019, clears $201A and $2018, then returns.
Stage is not 1: compares it with 2 and goes to stage_not2 $4EB3 if different.

Stage 2. When section_index ($0298) is below 2, reads two pointers from ($2A),$13 and ($2C),$13 into $E1/$E2, writes $36 at offsets $28 and $29 of that target, and sets $1D08/$1D0A to $A0 and $1D09/$1D0B to $00. Falls into stage2_common.
Stage 2 common part: clears bytes $1D6A and $1D6B. If section_index ($0298) is 6 or more, also sets $3914=$54 and $3915=$34.
Stage 2 end: stores $BD, $B7 and $BC at $30DA, $30CA and $30D6, then initialises a table at $BFFE-$C007 (values $FF, $00, $01, $06, $80 by byte) and returns with RTS.
Stage is not 2: compares it with 3 and goes to patch_stage_exit $4EDC if different.
Stage 3: stores $C0 at $1AD0, $00 at $1AD1, $10 at $1AE5, $04 at $1AE6, $19 at $BF22, $01 at $BF24 and $00 at $BF23/$BF25, then falls into the RTS.
Return point of patch_stage_code (RTS), also reached for stage 4 or higher where nothing is patched.

Resets per-round state: stores zero or $FF into about 30 game variables ($0898-$0914, $06-$1A, player_effect $08B1, player_hit $0292, jump_state $08FA, view_pinned_edges $08FE), loads section 0's record from table $0D22 indexed by $0C06 to get byte $18 into $16, marks every obj_state $3592-$35E5 as $FF (free), then runs the start-position lookup, spawns objects, and ends by jumping to player_pose $413A.
Loop: writes $FF into obj_state $3592,x for x = $53 down to 0, freeing 84 object slots.
Loop: zeroes the six bytes $06DD-$06E2.

Start of the per-record test: record pointer is $E1/$E2 (from stage tables $8113/$8118, read after writing $85 to the cartridge bank register $DE00). Compares player_hit_x $08E3/$08E4 and player_hit_y $08E5/$08E6 against the record's min and max x and y (bytes 0-7); any miss branches to skip_to_next_start_record.
Record did not contain the player position: scans forward from byte $10 for a byte with bit 7 set, adds that length to $E1/$E2, and retests the next record at find_start_record_loop.
Loop: advances Y until the byte at ($E1),y has bit 7 set, marking the end of the current record.
A record matched: copies bytes 8-11 to $1C-$1F, bytes 12-15 to player_x $08B7, player_x_hi $08B8, player_y $08B9, and player_y_hi $08BA, then reads byte 16 as the section index.

Stores the section index (bit 7 stripped; if bit 7 was set, $09 is first set to 2) into section_index $0298, then loads the section record pointer from table $0D22 into $26/$27 and reads two bytes from ($E9) into $F0 and $08CC.
Reads the next object-range pair from the matched record (from Y = $11 on): a first byte with bit 7 set ends the list; otherwise X = first index and $E3 = end index, with Y saved in $E4.
Loop: calls $8000 once for each X from the range start up to (not including) $E3, then restores Y from $E4 and goes back to next_spawn_range.
After the object ranges: sets $01 to $35, calls load_section_record $936E, sets $28/$29 to $B9C9 and $08FC to $38, and calls $0BF6.
Loop: sets $17 = $16 + 9, then for nine slots counting down from $17-1 writes $FF to obj_state $3592 and obj_move_bits $3484, and 1 to $3427.

Runs with interrupts off and $01 = $37 while cartridge bank $8D is selected: copies a 63-byte sprite shape into $FF80 when player_shape_3 $08EC differs from the cached value $02CB (source from tables $9245/$9263), the same for $08EA into $FF00 (cache $02CC, tables $91BF/$9202), and $08EB into $FF40 (cache $02CD); the code then restores bank $80 and $01 = $35. Note a spin loop at $50BB when $08EA is zero, seen in the disassembly.
First code the game runs from RAM (the hand-over, entry.vsf): clears $C480-$C53F, copies 192 bytes to $44E1 and selects bank 13.

Called by game_start ($8003). Disable interrupts, set $08B0 to $FF, point the NMI vector ($FFFA/$FFFB) at nmi_frame ($4D1D), switch the cartridge into view ($01 = $37), call $8194 (with the cartridge in view this runs the cartridge's code there, not the main loop's; facts.md has $0A9B use it to refresh the stack-page routines), copy six cartridge directory entries (0-5, per facts.md) into RAM with cart_copy_six, then hide the cartridge again ($01 = $35).
Keyboard matrix scan through CIA 1 ($DC00 rows, $DC01 columns), called from $80FC.

Draw the strip of the background that a one-tile scroll will bring into view. It does nothing unless scroll_phase ($0E) is zero. It then picks from scroll_dir ($0F: 0 is up, 2 right, 4 down, 6 left, and the odd numbers 1, 3, 5, and 7 are the diagonals between them) the row, the column, or both that are about to appear at the edge of the screen, and fills them into the off-screen character buffer whose address is in $08C1/$08C2. The stage map is read through the row pointer tables $2A and $2C (low and high bytes of each map row's address); each map byte is a tile, expanded to a 2 by 2 block of characters taken from the table at $2E/$2F, with $08C7 and $08C8 choosing which half of the tile the row or column starts in. A row is 40 characters (20 tiles) wide and a column 21 characters tall. The routines at $433D-$438B set $0F and clear $0E, $4B8A sets $0E to 1 once a tile step is made, and $888D then counts $0E down.

Refresh the colour RAM of the 21 playfield rows ($D800-$DB47, 840 characters) so it matches the screen buffer that is now on show. The screen buffer is swapped by the tile step at $4B8A, which flips $10 (0 shows the buffer at $C800, 1 shows $CC00; build_vic_shadows turns that into $D018 $21 or $31). Colour RAM exists only once, so it is rewritten rather than swapped: the tile step sets scroll_phase ($0E) to 1, and the countdown at $888D calls this routine when it sees the old value 1, one frame later. Each character's colour is taken from char_colour_table ($0C22). Reached by the jump at $889B and by the stub at $9517. The copy is unrolled, 32 characters per loop pass with Y as the index, in four loops (three pages of 256 characters and a last one of 72): recolour_c800_0 and the loops after it do the $C800 buffer, and recolour_cc00_0 and its loops do the $CC00 buffer.
Colour-RAM refresh from the screen buffer at $C800, used when $10 is zero. Clears carry for the additions in the loops and starts Y at 0.

First of 4 copy loops that read the screen buffer at $C800 one character at a time and write each character's colour to colour RAM. Each of the 32 unrolled steps takes the character code from $C800+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $D800+Y. Y then moves on by $20 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 256 characters, from $D800 to $D8FF. When Y wraps it falls into the next page's loop at $5CF6.

Copy loop 2 of 4 for the screen buffer at $C800. Each of the 32 unrolled steps takes the character code from $C900+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $D900+Y. Y then moves on by $20 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 256 characters, from $D900 to $D9FF. When Y wraps it falls into the next page's loop at $5E20.

Copy loop 3 of 4 for the screen buffer at $C800. Each of the 32 unrolled steps takes the character code from $CA00+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $DA00+Y. Y then moves on by $20 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 256 characters, from $DA00 to $DAFF. When Y wraps it falls into the next page's loop at $5F4C.

Copy loop 4 of 4 for the screen buffer at $C800. Each of the 36 unrolled steps takes the character code from $CA48+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $DA48+Y. Y then moves on by $24 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 72 characters, from $DB00 to $DB47 (the Y offsets are shifted so the unrolled steps end exactly at the last playfield character). That ends the 21 playfield rows (840 characters, $D800-$DB47); the routine then returns.

Colour-RAM refresh from the screen buffer at $CC00, used when $10 is non-zero (jumped to from $5BC6). Same four loops as recolour_c800 with the source moved up by $0400; clears carry and starts Y at 0.

First of 4 copy loops that read the screen buffer at $CC00 one character at a time and write each character's colour to colour RAM. Each of the 32 unrolled steps takes the character code from $CC00+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $D800+Y. Y then moves on by $20 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 256 characters, from $D800 to $D8FF. When Y wraps it falls into the next page's loop at $61C7.

Copy loop 2 of 4 for the screen buffer at $CC00. Each of the 32 unrolled steps takes the character code from $CD00+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $D900+Y. Y then moves on by $20 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 256 characters, from $D900 to $D9FF. When Y wraps it falls into the next page's loop at $62F1.

Copy loop 3 of 4 for the screen buffer at $CC00. Each of the 32 unrolled steps takes the character code from $CE00+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $DA00+Y. Y then moves on by $20 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 256 characters, from $DA00 to $DAFF. When Y wraps it falls into the next page's loop at $641D.

Copy loop 4 of 4 for the screen buffer at $CC00. Each of the 24 unrolled steps takes the character code from $CE48+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $DA48+Y. Y then moves on by $18 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 72 characters, from $DB00 to $DB47 (the Y offsets are shifted so the unrolled steps end exactly at the last playfield character). That ends the 21 playfield rows (840 characters, $D800-$DB47); the routine then returns.
Sound start-up: clears the filter resonance ($D417) and sets volume 15 with the low-pass filter ($D418 = $1F). The SID writes in the census all fall in $6615-$6ED4.

Sound driver setup: sets busy flag $6502 (incremented here, cleared at $6781), then copies six bytes from $70BA,x ($70BA-$70BF plus the caller's x) into $651B-$6520. Zeroes per-voice state for voices 2 to 0 in $6515-$65C5 and calls $693F for each. Clears SID registers $D400-$D417, sets the per-voice flags $FC-$FE to 1, and loads $650x-$651x counters with 1, 2, and 3. If $65C3 is zero, sets volume $65C2 and SID $D418 to $1F.

Loop over voices 2, 1, and 0 using counter $FF: zeroes the per-voice arrays ($6515, $658E, $656B, $6588, $65C5, $6576, $6579, $657C, $6582, $6585), calls $693F, then stores 2 and $66 in $6521-$652A, 0 in $6530 and $6548, and $F5/$F6 in $655C/$655F.
Writes $08 then $00 to each SID register $D400-$D417 counting x down from $17, leaving every register at zero.
Clears the busy flag $6502 and returns; reached directly when $65C3 is nonzero, skipping the volume setup.

Per-frame sound driver step: returns at once if busy flag $6502 is nonzero. Otherwise walks voices 2 to 0 (counter $FF), loading the SID register offset from $65FF,x into $656F, and skips voices whose flag $FC,x is zero. Per active voice: optional call to $6828 when $65C3 is set, volume fade via $65BF, then the step routines $684C, $6A09, $6CBE, $6D81, and the frequency write. Finishes with $6E3E and a jump to $6DCE.
Starts a pass: sets the voice counter $FF to 2.
Top of the per-voice loop: loads x from $FF, copies the voice's SID offset $65FF,x to $656F, and jumps to sid_next_voice if the voice flag $FC,x is zero.
Active voice: calls $6828 when $65C3 is nonzero.

If fade flag $65BF is nonzero, decrements delay $65C0; when it reaches zero, reloads it from $65C1, decrements volume $65C2, and writes it to SID $D418. Jumps to $6EB0 when the low nibble of the new volume is zero; otherwise continues.

Calls $684C, then skips to sid_next_voice if $FC,x is zero or $6582,x is nonzero. Otherwise calls $6A09, $6CBE, and $6D81, and skips to sid_next_voice if $657C,x is nonzero. When $6585,x is set, clears it and looks up the voice's frequency: y = $6568,x + $658B,x + $658E,x indexes the tables $6F06 (low byte, to $6562,x) and $6F64 (high byte, to $6565,x).
Calls $6D08, then writes the voice's frequency low byte $6562,x and high byte $6565,x to SID registers $D400,y and $D401,y, where y is the offset saved in $656F.
Decrements the voice counter $FF and loops back to $6791 until it goes negative.
After the last voice: calls $6E3E, then jumps to $6DCE.

Sort list for the logical sprites: an entry is filed at position Y / 2 of its screen line, or at the next free position after it, so walking the list from the start gives top-to-bottom order. A position whose value has bit 7 clear holds an entry number; $FF marks a free position, and $7F, written one past the highest position used, ends the list.
Start of a game: initialise, set the CIA 2 timer for the per-frame NMI, wait for raster line $EE, blank the screen and enter the stage.
A stage begins: stage_start loads it from the cartridge, then the round starts.

A round begins (at a stage's start and after losing a life): stop the interrupts, reset the frame state, count $089D down (below $C1 the game is over: $BD5D, then back to the title at $4000), start the sound, set the raster interrupt to irq_panel at line $DE, set up the stage, then wait 20 frames.

The main loop, once a frame: count the frame, scan the keyboard ($5290) for as long as $02CA holds the game paused, run the game's updates ($A178 to $5B83), count down $0293 after a life is lost and restart the round at 0, then wait for the frame.

Main-loop call of place_player_sprites. The auto label f_8113 comes from two reads of the table of stage pointers in bank 0 at $8113 ($0B46 and $4F6C, with the cartridge bank 0 switched in by $DE00); nothing in RAM writes to this instruction, so the call is never patched.
Wait for the interrupt to set frame_flag, then choose next frame's raster interrupt and copy the sprite tables at $07B4-$07E6 into the set the interrupts draw from.

Wait for frame_flag to change once more, clear it and allow interrupts, then check for a cleared stage (bit 5 of $3592 at the current position $08CC): if so, increment stage and play the stage-clear sequence.

Raster interrupt at line $D5, the top of the status panel. Waits for line $D6, then sets $D011 = $57: extended colour and multicolour together, a mode the VIC-II shows as black, which hides the switch to the panel's video bank ($DD00 = $02), screen and character set ($D018 = $FF) and colours. Moves all sprites to x = 0, out of sight, chains irq_panel_on for line $DE, and calls sound_frame.

Once a frame, update the pool of nine short-lived objects, objects temp_first ($16) to temp_first + 8 (stage 1 starts with $4C-$54; the setup loop at $5066 sets their obj_state to $FF, meaning unused), from the last slot down. The pool slot number is kept in Y, and Y also indexes four velocity bytes ($3FD3, $3FDC, $3FE5, $3FEE: X low and high, Y low and high) and a life counter ($3FF7) beside the object tables. For each slot not retired: when bit 7 of $35EF is set it makes the object blink, clearing bit 6 of $35EF on frames whose parity matches bit 0 of $35EF and setting it on the others; the object moves only on frames where $3484 shares a bit with move_mask. A move counts the life down by one (at zero the slot is retired with $A0), adds the velocity to the position, and applies object_arc_step ($88CE) when $3F19 is non-zero. If bit 3 of obj_state is set it then calls $9400 with A = $0C and Y = $0A (probably a stage-map test); when the result has either of its low two bits set, the object is retired, or, when bit 2 of obj_state is set, it turns into a short animation instead (bits 2 and 3 of obj_state cleared and bit 0 set, frame $37, life $18, velocity and $3F19 cleared) and the routine returns at once, leaving the lower slots for the next frame. Otherwise it calls $B57A and tests the new box against the view window ($40-$47): an object left of, right of, or below the view is retired, and one above it is retired only when $3F19 is zero. A survivor's position is stored and its hit box set by set_object_hitbox ($ABC7). Whether these are enemy shots, debris, or both has not been checked.

Once a frame, read the joystick and run the player. It writes $7F to both CIA 1 ports, reads port A (port B instead when A reads $7F), keeps the low four bits in joy_bits ($08), and copies the fire bit (bit 4) into bit 6 of $08C6 (1 means not pressed). Before that it tests a hidden combination: when port A ($DC00, joystick 2) has bits 0 and 4 low (up and fire) and port B ($DC01, joystick 1) has bits 1 and 4 low (down and fire), it increments cheat_flag ($08F9) and the background colour ($D021), once for each frame they are held. With port A at $7F the keys left arrow and space also pull port B bits 1 and 4 low. It then decrements $08DE unless its bit 7 is set, saves the previous position with save_player_x and save_player_y, runs player_mode_step ($85DC), sets $19 to $FF, calls $AF34 (skipped while bit 6 of $08C6 is set), $98F3, and $9F05 (skipped while bit 7 of $08C6 is set), picks the animation frame with player_pose ($413A), and ends in $92DF.

Run the player's movement for the current player_mode ($09). Mode 1 goes to $9025, and modes other than 0 and 1 go to $8E88. Mode 0 first rewrites $08C6: $40 when fire is not pressed (bit 6 set), otherwise $00 while $08FA is non-zero and $80 when it is zero; then it runs $8603, which reads joy_bits, and goes on to $89A9.

Mode 0 movement for one frame, called from player_mode_step. Reads joy_bits ($08), fire_flags ($08C6), and jump_state ($08FA). While player_hit ($0292) is non-zero it goes to player_hit_step. Calls $8D67 unless $1A is negative. On the ground: down ($0D) goes to player_down_enter_mode1, right ($07) to player_walk_right, left ($0B) to player_walk_left, down-right ($05) and down-left ($09) to player_down_right and player_down_left (or to player_stop_facing when $0C is non-zero and bit 7 of $08C6 is set), up-right ($06) and up-left ($0A) to the jump routines (walks instead while bit 7 of $08C6 is set), and up ($0E) to player_jump_up. In the air only right and left count. Anything else sets move_dir ($0D) to $FF and $0299 to 0, then runs player_jump_motion when airborne or sets $0905 to 1 when on the ground.

Start a jump to the right (joy_bits $06). When jump_state ($08FA) is non-zero it goes to walk_right_dir instead. Otherwise it calls $42F8 (adds move_step to player_prev_x, skipped while bit 7 of $08C6 is set), loads A with 6, and falls into player_jump_start.

Shared tail of the jumps: stores A in move_dir ($0D), calls $0B8C with A at 0, and clears bit 7 of obj_flags ($364C) for the object whose index is in $1A when $1A is not negative. Then sets $1A and jump_state ($08FA) to $FF, $0299 and $0C to 0, $0903 to 1, and $0905 to 3, and copies $08FC into jump_counter ($08FB). player_jump_motion then lifts the player by $02CE steps until jump_counter runs out.

Start a jump to the left (joy_bits $0A). When jump_state ($08FA) is non-zero it goes to walk_left_dir instead. Otherwise it calls $42E1 (subtracts move_step from player_prev_x, skipped while bit 7 of $08C6 is set), loads A with $0A, and goes to player_jump_start.

Down-left on the ground, entered with A at $09. Stores A in move_dir ($0D) and $18, sets $0B to 1 and $0905 to 5, and loads A with $FF, then joins player_walk_left at walk_left_move, so $0299 becomes $FF and the player steps left.

Down-right on the ground, entered with A at $05. Stores A in move_dir ($0D) and $18, sets $0B to 1 and $0905 to 5, and loads A with $FF, then joins player_walk_right at walk_right_move, so $0299 becomes $FF and the player steps right.

Step right. On the ground ($08FA zero) it sets $0905 to 1. Sets move_dir ($0D) to $07 and $0299 to 0, then calls $42F8, which adds move_step ($0A) to player_prev_x unless bit 7 of $08C6 is set. When $0C is non-zero it goes to player_slope_step. Otherwise it sets move_step to 2 and, when jump_state is non-zero, goes on to player_jump_motion.

Step left. On the ground ($08FA zero) it sets $0905 to 1. Sets move_dir ($0D) to $0B and $0299 to 0, then calls $42E1, which subtracts move_step ($0A) from player_prev_x unless bit 7 of $08C6 is set. When $0C is non-zero it goes to player_slope_step. Otherwise it sets move_step to 2 and, when jump_state is non-zero, goes on to player_jump_motion.

Vertical step that goes with a horizontal one when $0C is non-zero (A holds $0C). Ends in $430F (subtracts move_step from player_prev_y) or $4326 (adds it), whichever the direction calls for, and the rts of that routine returns to the caller, so no jump motion follows. With $0C equal to 1 the player goes down when bit 3 of move_dir ($0D) is set (moving left) and up when it is clear (moving right). With any other value it goes up when moving left and down when moving right.

Movement after a hit (player_hit non-zero). Does nothing while $0293 is non-zero. While jump_state ($08FA) is negative, or while $08ED plus $0F (added without clearing the carry first) is below $EB, it goes to player_jump_motion. Otherwise it sets $0293 to $19, the countdown that the main loop at $8122 uses to reach round_start.

Vertical motion of a jump, using jump_state ($08FA) and jump_counter ($08FB) on player_prev_y ($08BD/$08BE). A jump_state of 0 does nothing. A negative one (rising) clears bit 0 of move_dir ($0D), subtracts $02CE[x] from player_prev_y, where x is jump_counter limited to 16, and subtracts the same amount from jump_counter. When jump_counter would reach zero or below it sets jump_state to 1 and jump_counter to 0. A positive one (falling) clears bit 1 of move_dir, adds $02DF[x] with x as jump_counter, and raises jump_counter by one until it reaches 8.

Down pressed on the ground. Goes to player_stop when bit 7 of $08C6 is set. Otherwise it calls $9E69 and goes to player_stop when bit 4 of $08E9 is clear. Otherwise it sets $0322 to $12, adds $15 to player_y ($08B9/$08BA), adds $E1/$E2 to player_x ($08B7/$08B8), sets $08FF to $44, clears player_third_on ($0913), $0B, $0900, and $0323, sets player_mode ($09) to 1 and move_step ($0A) to 2, stores $0D in both $18 and move_dir ($0D), and sets $0905 to 6.
Stores A in $18, then runs player_stop. Reached from player_move with A at $05 or $09 when $0C is non-zero and bit 7 of $08C6 is set.
Stand still: sets move_dir ($0D) and $0299 to $FF and $0905 to 4. No position changes.
Start a straight-up jump (joy_bits $0E). When jump_state ($08FA) is non-zero it goes to player_jump_motion. Otherwise it loads A with $0E and goes to player_jump_start, with no horizontal step.

Set up the tables for a stage, called at $8049. Clears section_index ($0298), sets the sprite multicolour enable $D01C to $FF, and copies the 22 bytes at $0C0C-$0C21 to $2A-$3F. Points $24/$25 at $0D22 and loads $26/$27 from the word stored there. Copies $0C03, $0C04, and $0C05 to bg_colour0, bg_colour1, and bg_colour2 ($08C3-$08C5, written to the three VIC background colour registers by the raster routine at $4DB1), and sets the sprite multicolours $D025 and $D026 to $0B and $0F.

Count scroll_phase ($0E) down once a frame (called from the main loop at $825F). Does nothing when scroll_phase is negative. Otherwise it decrements it. When the old value was 1 it jumps to $5BC2. When the old value was 0 (now $FF) and player_hit ($0292) is zero, it reads the address from the tables $0324 (low) and $032C (high) at the index scroll_dir ($0F), stores it in $E1/$E2, and jumps through it at jump_via_e1. Any other old value just returns.

Jump through the address in $E1/$E2 (jmp ($00E1)). scroll_phase_step runs into it, and a jsr to it (as at $B224, after loading $E1/$E2 from the tables at $B33C and $B35F) lets the target's rts return to the caller.

Build the copies of the VIC registers that the raster routine at $4DAB-$4DCC writes out. shadow_d018 ($07B0, for $D018) gets $21 when $10 is zero and $31 otherwise. shadow_d016 ($07AF, for $D016) gets $10 combined with scroll_fine_x ($06). shadow_d011 ($07AE, for $D011) gets $10 combined with scroll_fine_y ($07). Called at $8191.

Apply one frame of vertical motion to an object's new position (E9/EA) according to obj_arc_state ($3F19 for the object in X, passed in the flags). With bit 7 and bit 6 set it falls: the position moves down by a value from $02DF indexed by obj_arc_counter ($3F76), which rises by one up to 8 (so it speeds up). With bit 7 set and bit 6 clear it rises by a value from $02CE indexed by the counter (at most 16), the counter falls by the same amount, and when it runs out obj_arc_state becomes $C0 (falling). With bit 7 clear it works out a move along a path through the data at the pointer $32 and, for a follower, stores the offset from its parent in $36F4 and $3748; that path is not decoded.

Path case of object_arc_step (obj_arc_state has bit 7 clear). Saves X (the object) in $EB and Y in $ED, calls path_advance with A as obj_arc_state, and restores X and Y. When bit 6 of obj_flags ($364C) is set it then stores $E7 minus $08DA in obj_off_x ($36F4) and $E9 minus $08DC in obj_off_y ($3748).

Advance an object one step along its path. A is obj_arc_state (an offset into the table of path addresses at the pointer $32) and X is the object. Loads $E3/$E4 with the word at $32 plus A, copies obj_arc_counter ($3F76) into $EC, and uses that as the slot in path_end ($5C), path_axes ($60), and path_pos ($64). When path_end is below path_pos the path is over (path_finish). Otherwise path_axes 0 adds one word of path data to the X position $E7/$E8, 1 adds one word to the Y position $E9/$EA, and 2 or more adds an X word then a Y word, reading at offset path_pos.

Add the next word of path data to the Y position $E9/$EA. The data is at $E3/$E4 plus Y; a low byte of $80 restarts at offset 0. Y is advanced by two and stored in path_pos ($64) at the slot in $EC. Entered by path_advance when path_axes is 1, and after path_add_x when it is 2 or more.

Add the next word of path data to the X position $E7/$E8. The data is at $E3/$E4 plus Y; a low byte of $80 restarts at offset 0. Y is advanced by two and stored in path_pos ($64) at the slot in $EC. Called by path_advance, which enters it directly when path_axes is 0.
End of a path: clears obj_arc_state ($3F19) for the object in $EB and returns.

Second half of mode 0 movement, reached from player_move. Checks the new position that player_move left in player_prev_x and player_prev_y against the blocks. While player_hit ($0292) is non-zero it goes to restore_player_pos ($4246). On the ground (jump_state $08FA zero) it looks at move_dir ($0D): with bit 3 clear it goes to collide_ground_right, with bit 3 set and bit 2 clear to collide_ground_left, and otherwise it returns. In the air it goes by move_dir: $05 to air_down_right_x, $09 to air_down_left_x, $0D to air_vertical, $0E to $8D10, $06 to $8CDF, and $0A to $8CF6. Any other value returns.

Ground check for a step to the left (move_dir with bit 3 set and bit 2 clear). When slope_kind ($0C) is non-zero it goes to $8C60. Otherwise it calls $9BF6, merges $E1, $E2, and $E3 into $E1, and tests bit 0 (solid). If it is set, save_player_x ($4263) copies player_x over player_prev_x, so the step is dropped. If it is clear, restore_player_x ($4249) copies player_prev_x into player_x, so the step stands. Either way it goes on to ground_floor_check.

Check what is under the player after a ground step. Returns at once when stand_obj ($1A) is not negative. Otherwise it calls $9D3C. If bit 5 is set in all three of $E1, $E2, and $E3, it clears $08FF, sets $0B, player_mode ($09), and move_step ($0A) to 1, 1, and 2, sets $0905 to 5, and returns (the player enters mode 1). Otherwise, if $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set, it stores those two bits shifted down in slope_kind ($0C). If no block has bit 0 set it starts a fall instead: jump_counter ($08FB) becomes 1, $0299 becomes 0, jump_state ($08FA) becomes 1, and $0905 becomes 3.

Ground check for a step to the right (move_dir with bit 3 clear). Same as collide_ground_left, but a non-zero slope_kind ($0C) goes to $8CAB and the block probe is $9C1E. A solid block drops the step through ground_x_blocked, and a free one commits it with restore_player_x ($4249) before going on to ground_floor_check.

Airborne step down and to the left (move_dir $09). Pushes $031D, subtracts the fall step $02DF[jump_counter] from it, calls $9BF6 with the smaller value, and puts $031D back. Then it merges $E1, $E2, and $E3 and tests bit 0. A solid block drops the step with save_player_x ($4263), and a free one commits it with restore_player_x ($4249). Both ways it ends in air_vertical.
Airborne step down and to the right (move_dir $05). Same as air_down_left_x, but the block probe is $9C1E instead of $9BF6. Both ways it ends in air_vertical.
Vertical check for an airborne player: calls air_floor_check, then goes on to $8D20.

Decide what the blocks under an airborne player do, then commit or adjust player_prev_y. First it calls $9D3C and merges $E1, $E2, and $E3. If bit 5 is set in all three, it sets $0905 to 5, $0B and player_mode ($09) to 1, ORs 3 into $18, copies $18 to move_dir ($0D), and goes to land_and_snap (mode 1 is entered). Otherwise, with bit 1 set in the merged value it goes to air_hit_hazard. If $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set it goes to $8C0B. When stand_obj ($1A) is not negative it goes to air_on_object. Otherwise bit 0 (solid) goes to air_land_solid. With bit 0 clear and bit 6 set it sets player_mode to 2, jump_state to $FF, jump_counter to $30, and $0905 to 7. In all other cases it commits the new Y with restore_player_y ($4256).

Land on a stage object: sets $0905 to 1, calls player_land, and sets player_prev_y to obj_hit_top for the object stand_obj ($1A), minus $031C and $031D. Then it commits the Y with restore_player_y ($4256).

Harmful block under the player (bit 1 set): sets player_hit ($0292) to 1, jump_state ($08FA) to $FF, and jump_counter ($08FB) to $10. Sound $24 is queued with queue_sound ($0B8C), and when $DF is non-zero sound $25 is also started through $6ED8. Then it goes to $8E2F.

Landing on a solid block. When up is held (bit 0 of joy_bits $08 clear) and fire is not pressed (bit 6 of fire_flags $08C6 set), the player jumps again at once: jump_state ($08FA) becomes $FF, jump_counter ($08FB) is loaded from $08FC, sound 0 is queued, and $0905 becomes 3. Otherwise $0905 becomes 1 and player_land runs. Either way it continues in snap_player_to_block.

Snap the player's feet to a block boundary. Adds $031C and $031D to player_prev_y ($08BD/$08BE), rounds the sum down to a multiple of $10, subtracts $031D and $031C again, and stores the result in player_prev_y. Then it commits the Y with restore_player_y ($4256).
Mark the player as on the ground: jump_state ($08FA) and slope_kind ($0C) become 0, and $0902 and move_dir ($0D) become $FE.

Slope check for an airborne player, entered from air_floor_check when $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set. When bit 0 of $0291 is set it goes straight to air_slope_land. Otherwise it takes (player_prev_x $08BB plus $1F) AND $0F into $E2, and turns that into $0F minus itself when bit 3 of $0291 is clear. Then it compares ((player_prev_y $08BD AND $0E) plus 1 plus $031C plus $031D) AND $0F with $E2. If that is smaller it goes to air_slope_commit, because the feet are still above the slope. If not, it falls into air_slope_land.

Land on a slope from the air: move_dir ($0D) becomes $FF, jump_state ($08FA) becomes 0, slope_kind ($0C) becomes 1 when bit 2 of $0291 is set and 2 otherwise, and $0905 becomes 1. Then player_prev_y ($08BD/$08BE) is increased by 1 and it falls into air_slope_commit.
Commit the step: goes to restore_player_pos ($4246), which copies player_prev_x and player_prev_y into player_x and player_y.

Ground step to the left while slope_kind ($0C) is non-zero, entered from collide_ground_left. When slope_kind is 1 it goes to ground_slope_left_one. Otherwise it calls $9D3C and, if $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set (still on a slope), goes to ground_slope_commit. If not, it adds 6 to player_prev_y ($08BD/$08BE) and goes to land_and_snap.

Ground step to the right with slope_kind ($0C) not equal to 1, reached from ground_slope_right. Calls $9D3C and, if $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set, goes to ground_slope_commit. Otherwise it goes to land_and_snap with player_prev_y unchanged.

Ground step to the left with slope_kind ($0C) equal to 1, reached from ground_slope_left. Calls $9D3C and, if $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set, goes to ground_slope_commit. Otherwise, unless bit 1 of joy_bits ($08) is set, it sets $0905 and $0B to 5. Either way it ends in land_and_snap.

Ground step to the right while slope_kind ($0C) is non-zero, entered from collide_ground_right. When slope_kind is not 1 it goes to ground_slope_right_two. Otherwise it calls $9D3C and, if $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set, goes to ground_slope_commit. If not, it adds 6 to player_prev_y ($08BD/$08BE) and, unless bit 1 of joy_bits ($08) is set, sets $0905 and $0B to 5. It ends in land_and_snap.
Commit the step: goes to restore_player_pos ($4246). Used by the ground slope routines when $0291 still has bit 2 or bit 3 set.

Airborne step up and to the right (move_dir $06). Calls $9C1E. When bit 0 is set in $E1, $E2, or $E3 the step is dropped with save_player_x ($4263); otherwise it is committed with restore_player_x ($4249). Both ways it ends in air_up_check.
Airborne step up and to the left (move_dir $0A). Same as air_up_right_x, but the block probe is $9BF6 instead of $9C1E. Both ways it ends in air_up_check.

Vertical check for an airborne player moving up. Calls $9D17 and merges $E1, $E2, and $E3. When bit 0 is set it goes to air_start_fall. Otherwise it commits the Y with restore_player_y ($4256), calls $9E69, and goes on to air_mode1_check. Also entered with move_dir $0E.

Calls $9E69, then tests bit 4 of $08E8 and $08E9; when either is clear it returns. When both are set it adds $E1/$E2 to player_x ($08B7/$08B8), sets $0B, $08FF, and jump_state ($08FA) to 0, player_mode ($09) to 1, move_step ($0A) to 2, $18 and move_dir ($0D) to $0E, and $0905 to 6 (the player enters mode 1). Entered from air_up_check, and from air_vertical.
Start a fall: jump_state ($08FA) becomes 1, jump_counter ($08FB) becomes 0, and it returns.

Carry the player along with the object it stands on; player_move calls it with X as stand_obj ($1A) when that is not negative. It acts on $19: $0E goes to ride_up, $0D to ride_down, $0B to ride_left, $07 to ride_right, and any other value returns. Each case moves player_prev_x or player_prev_y, tests the blocks, and commits with restore_player_x ($4249) or restore_player_y ($4256) before ending in ride_finish.
Case $0E of player_ride_object: calls place_player_on_object, commits the Y with restore_player_y ($4256), and goes to ride_finish.

Case $0D of player_ride_object. When $0295 is 7 or more it goes to player_leave_object. Otherwise it calls place_player_on_object and $9D3C and merges $E1, $E2, and $E3. With bit 1 set it goes to ride_hit; if not, it commits the Y with restore_player_y ($4256) and goes to ride_finish.
The player leaves the object: $0299 becomes 0, jump_state ($08FA) becomes 1, jump_counter ($08FB) becomes 8, and $0905 and $0903 become 3.

Case $0B of player_ride_object. Subtracts obj_speed ($34E1) for the object in X from player_prev_x ($08BB/$08BC), calls $9BF6, and merges $E1, $E2, and $E3. With bit 0 set the step is not committed and it goes to ride_finish. Otherwise it commits with restore_player_x ($4249) and, when stand_obj ($1A) is not negative, goes to ride_finish; else it returns.
Case $07 of player_ride_object. Same as ride_left, but it adds obj_speed ($34E1) to player_prev_x, and the block probe is $9C1E instead of $9BF6.
End of a ride step: clears bit 7 of obj_flags ($364C) for the object stand_obj ($1A) and calls $AC13. When stand_obj is still not negative it returns; otherwise it goes to player_leave_object.

Harmful block while riding an object (bit 1 set): sets player_hit ($0292) to 1, jump_state ($08FA) to $FF, and jump_counter ($08FB) to $10. Sound $24 is queued with queue_sound ($0B8C), and when $DF is non-zero sound $25 is also started through $6ED8. It falls into hit_save_pos.

Remember where the player was hit: stores player_x ($08B7/$08B8) in player_hit_x ($08E3/$08E4) and player_y ($08B9/$08BA) in player_hit_y ($08E5/$08E6). A word whose high byte is negative is stored as 0. Reached by falling in from ride_hit and by a jump from air_hit_hazard.

Put the player on the object in X: stores the object's Y position (obj_y_lo $39A6 and obj_y_hi $3A03) minus $031D and then minus $031C in player_prev_y ($08BD/$08BE). It loads Y from stand_obj ($1A) but does not use it. The caller commits the Y with restore_player_y ($4256).

Mode 2 movement for one frame, jumped to from player_mode_step for any player_mode ($09) other than 0 and 1. Keeps only bit 6 of fire_flags ($08C6), so bit 7 is clear and the position steps are never skipped, sets player_action ($0905) to 7, runs mode2_move ($8E9B) to pick and apply the direction, and goes to mode2_collide ($8F73) to check the new position.

Choose the direction in mode 2 and step player_prev_x or player_prev_y. Sets move_dir ($0D) to $FF first. While jump_state ($08FA) is non-zero it runs mode2_jump_motion ($8F12) and then steps sideways by the facing flag $18: bit 3 clear steps right ($0D masked with $07, then $42F8), bit 3 set steps left ($0D masked with $0B, then $42E1). When jump_state is zero it follows joy_bits ($08): $07 is right, $0B left, $0E up ($430F), and $0D down ($4326), and the diagonals $06, $05, $09, and $0A do one vertical step and one horizontal step. The joy_bits value is stored in move_dir; any other value leaves $FF.

Vertical motion of the mode 2 jump, the reverse of player_jump_motion, using jump_state ($08FA) and jump_counter ($08FB) on player_prev_y ($08BD/$08BE). A jump_state of 0 does nothing. A negative one clears bit 1 of move_dir ($0D), adds $02CE[x] to player_prev_y, where x is jump_counter limited to 16, and subtracts the same amount from jump_counter; when jump_counter would reach zero or below, jump_state becomes 1 and jump_counter 0. A positive one clears bit 0 of move_dir, subtracts $02DF[x] with x as jump_counter, and then adds one to jump_counter, or sets jump_state to 0 when x is 8 or more. Mode 2 is entered with $FF and $30, so the player first moves down the screen and then back up.

Second half of mode 2 movement, reached from player_mode2_step. While jump_state ($08FA) is non-zero it commits player_prev_y with $4256 without a block test, then probes the sideways step ($9BF6 when bit 3 of move_dir ($0D) is set, otherwise $9C1E). When bit 0 is clear in $E1, $E2, and $E3 it commits X with $4249; otherwise it flips bits 2 and 3 of move_dir and stores the result in move_dir and $18, which turns the player round. On the ground it returns while move_dir is negative; otherwise it probes left or right the same way, commits X with $4249 or cancels it with save_player_x ($4263), then handles up ($0D bit 0 clear, probe $9D17) and down (bit 1 clear, probe $9D3C). A block with bit 0 set stops the step; otherwise it commits Y with $4256. Going up with bit 6 clear in the probe results also sets player_mode ($09) to 0, jump_state to $FF, jump_counter ($08FB) to $08FC plus $10, and player_action ($0905) to 3.

Mode 1 movement for one frame, jumped to from player_mode_step when player_mode ($09) is 1. When $08FF is non-zero it goes straight to mode1_collide ($919E). Otherwise it rewrites fire_flags ($08C6), first setting $0903 to $FF when bits 7 and 6 are both set, then keeping bit 6 and setting bit 7 when bit 6 is clear. Then it runs mode1_move_vertical ($9055) when $0B is zero or mode1_move_horizontal ($917A) otherwise, and goes to mode1_collide.

Mode 1 movement when $0B is zero. Returns at once while bit 7 of fire_flags ($08C6) is set. Sets player_action ($0905) to 6, and sets jump_state ($08FA) to $FF when bits 2 and 3 of joy_bits ($08) are both set. While jump_state is not negative only up ($0E, step with $430F) and down ($0D, step with $4326) count; any other joy_bits value sets move_dir ($0D) to $FF. With jump_state negative, up and down work the same way, and left or right (diagonals included) sets move_dir to $0B or $07, moves player_prev_x by 4 that way, and probes with $9BF6 or $9C1E. When bit 0 is clear in $E1, $E2, and $E3 it sets player_mode ($09) to 0, player_third_on ($0913) to 1, and queues sound 0 with queue_sound ($0B8C); otherwise up and down apply.
Return in A the smallest of the eight bytes of spr_free_line ($07CF-$07D6), one per hardware sprite slot. Called from $8147. Each slot is compared with the running minimum, starting from slot 0.

Start an object on a path from a four-byte record at ($E3),Y. X is the object. Y is advanced past the first byte, then the next bytes go to obj_arc_state ($3F19,X) and obj_arc_counter ($3F76,X, the slot in the path tables). The third byte is kept in $ED and the fourth is stored in path_end ($5C), $ED in path_axes ($60), and 0 in path_pos ($64), all at that slot. Y is restored from $EB and the routine returns with carry set. No caller was found in the stage 1 snapshot; stage code that is not loaded may call it.

Mode 1 movement when $0B is non-zero. Sets player_action ($0905) to 5. Right in joy_bits ($08, bit 3 clear) sets move_dir ($0D) to $07 and steps right with $42F8; otherwise left (bit 2 clear) sets $0B and steps left with $42E1; otherwise move_dir becomes $FF.

Second half of mode 1 movement, reached from player_mode1_step. When $08FF is negative it is set to 0, and when it is positive nothing more happens. When $08FF is zero and $0B is non-zero, move_dir ($0D) of $07 goes to $9276 and $0B to $92AD. When $0B is zero, $0E goes to mode1_up_end ($91CF), $0D to $91EB, and left (bit 2 clear) or right (bit 3 clear) to $9207 or $921C, which move player_x by 8 and start a jump back in mode 0. mode1_up_end probes with $9D17; when $0291 is non-zero it commits Y with $4256, otherwise it sets player_third_on ($0913) to 0, $0903 to 1, and $08FF to 2.

Last step of update_player. First it updates the energy bar: when $08CB is non-zero it takes the low 5 bits of the health of object $08CC into $08A1 and draws the bar with $831B; when $08CB is zero and player_hit ($0292) is zero it calls update_view_scroll ($470C). Then, while the player is not hit, it takes a probe point (player_x plus $18, and player_y plus $031C, with their high bytes $08B8 and $08BA) and finds the stage section that holds it. The current section record is the one at ($26) and the section number is section_index ($0298); $93CD tests the point against the bounds in the record (offsets $0E to $15: x low and high, then y low and high, each as two bytes). When the point is outside, it tries the next section (up to the limit $0C06) and then the previous one, using the record addresses at $0D22, and on a match stores the new index and pointer and falls into $936E.

Copy the settings of the section record at ($26) into working variables: bytes 0 to 5 to $0908, $0909, $0906, $0907, $090A, and $090B, byte $16 to $08FD, and bytes $17 and $18 to obj_first and obj_end. $08FE is cleared, and bit 2 of $08FD is cleared unless it is set and the low two bits of $08FD differ from $08A7, in which case those bits are stored in $08A7 and bits 2 and 3 of $08FD are set. Called when the player enters a new section, and from $5048 during stage setup. What the individual settings mean is not yet known.

Test whether the point at $E1/$E2 (x) and $E3/$E4 (y) lies inside the section record at ($E5): it compares each coordinate with the 16-bit minimum and maximum at offsets $0E to $15. Returns with the carry set when the point is inside and clear when it is outside.

Look up the block property at a position. The inputs are A (added to the x position $E7/$E8), Y (added to the y position $E9/$EA), and the 16-bit position itself. Both are divided by 16 to give a block column ($EB) and row ($EC); the row picks a row pointer from the tables at ($2A) and ($2C), the column picks a block number from that row, and the block number picks the property byte in the table at ($30), which comes back in A. A row above the top of the map ($EA negative) returns 0. Used by the object code at $84B5 and $AA3C; the same lookup idea gives the tile bits that the player code tests (for example bit 0 solid and bit 1 harmful).

Copy the logical sprite list into the hardware sprite tables ($07B4-$07E6) in top-to-bottom order. It starts at slot 0, or slot 1 when place_third_sprite already used slot 0 (spr_enable $07B2 non-zero). It walks sprite_y_buckets ($7CBD) from the top: positions with bit 7 set are skipped, $7F ends the list, any other value is a logical sprite number, and each position it consumes (the $7F included) is reset to $FF. For each sprite it copies the pointer ($0838) to spr_pointer ($07C7), the colour ($0808) to spr_colour ($07B4), and the X low ($0850) and Y ($0880) to the X and Y pair at $07D7/$07D8 (two bytes per slot); it sets the slot's bit in spr_x_msb ($07B1) when the X high byte ($0868) is non-zero; and it sets spr_free_line ($07CF) to Y + $16, or Y + $2B when the colour's bit 7 is set, in which case the slot's bit is also set in spr_expand ($07B3). It stops after eight slots, leaving in sprite_more ($6B) the list position of the last sprite copied, or at the end of the list, leaving 0 there. Then it sets spr_enable from the table at $02A6 (one bit for each slot used). wait_nmi uses $6B to choose the raster interrupt at $95A4 when it is non-zero.
